scope: Read-only native bob001 numeric capture, local first-person pawn and HUD sway
observations: All reconstructable single-slot history writes select an exact existing endpoint at new sample time minus 1/16 second. No bracket selection occurs in this window.
All history timestamps are exact multiples of 1/64 second. Every reconstructable write replaces the oldest timestamp.

Every reconstructed cached rate matches float32 wrapped difference between newly written and selected history angles, multiplied by 16. The prediction interpolation flag is true throughout the captured window.
Every observed HUD update matches float32 elapsed-global-time smoothing: alpha=clamp(15*(new timestamp-old timestamp),0,1), then smooth+=(target-smooth)*alpha.
All observed HUD updates share the sampled global current time and copy the sampled pawn rate as their target.
Global current time changes between frame phases, including backward transitions. It is not one monotonically advancing render clock.
inferences: The normal captured history path writes at a 64 Hz time grid and reads the exact endpoint four ticks earlier. Polling cannot determine the count of duplicate native invocations between state changes.

Early-frame observations commonly expose an integer history time, while the HUD-updated observation exposes a fractional global time. This corroborates phase-dependent global clocks without identifying every call site.

The unusual quaternion interpolation quotient is real in the separate native oracle but unused in this captured sequence; do not replace it with conventional interpolation or claim all runtime inputs avoid it.
remainingRuntimeMetadata: Invocation trace or equivalent coherent samples of player-time accessor, source-angle interpolation inputs and history before/after each writer call.
Different render cadence and special-state samples before claiming the observed endpoint path is universal.

For camera kick: selected input-history entry and attack index, resolver path/cache, exact sampler current time, command anchor, and presented-frame identity at each shot. The current motion stream does not include them.
limits: Read-only polling can miss native calls. A observed history transition is not proof that exactly one invocation occurred.
Sampler verifies frame/HUD state stability, but pawn source/history/rate fields are separate reads. Mismatches may be mixed phases or missed transitions.
The player-time accessor branch is not sampled directly; a newly written sample time is an observed writer output.
Reconstructing a previous four-slot state is justified only for the single-slot changes included; multiple-slot changes are separately counted.
This stream has no firing command-history indices, camera punch anchor or presented-frame ring payload. It cannot alone close earlier shot-anchor clock mapping.
A sampler records only changes to frame counter or HUD motion state; unrelated pawn-only transitions can be skipped.
A native state match is not a rendered placement/handedness comparison and does not establish screen-space parity.
The initial observation does not expose construction, equip, respawn or teleport reset behavior.
